retained_owner_paragraphs_verbatim:
SPEED (owner, 2026-11-10: Codex tokens are plentiful; wall-clock time is the constraint) 
- Run up to 8 bounded workers at a time, as separate `codex exec` processes. Use a smaller model or medium 
  reasoning for producers, extraction and formatting. Keep Very High only for yourself: legal judgment, 
  control adjudication and integration. Give deterministic work to scripts. 
- In your first ten minutes, dispatch any source fetches your pool needs, so they finish while you produce. 
- Prepare the next batch while the current one is under review. Never leave the pipeline idle waiting 
  on one step. 
- [OWNER OVERRIDE — the owner keeps or deletes this paragraph] Dollars are not your limit for this wave. 
  Still log spend in COSTS.log and run the Bentham gate after every batch. Treat an economic STOP (lower 
  yield per dollar than the next action) as advice, not a halt, while unattempted orders remain in your 
  pool. Stop a pool only for quality: any missed planted control, or two batches in a row with zero filed.

SHARED RULES (identical in every lane's prompt) 
- This wave produces dossiers. It builds no tools, pilots, surveys, dashboards, workflows or 
  infrastructure, and never edits .github/. If a defect blocks production: record it in Kean, route around 
  it, and only if it blocks many orders fix it with the smallest change in its own PR. 
- Start by reading HANDOFF/KEAN.md, HANDOFF/NEWEST.md, jobs/bentham/output/PLAN.md, 
  jobs/carnot-coordinator/PROTOCOL.md and jobs/claim-kit/AGENT_PROTOCOL.md. Before building or trying 
  anything, run `python -I jobs/kean/kean.py search <words>`. 
- Isolation: work only in your own worktree, created from origin/main under 
  C:\Users\danie\eo-wt\mommsen-<n> (sparse; name the folders you need). Never work in 
  C:\Users\danie\Projects\Executive-Orders (a stale checkout). 
  - Branch prefix codex/mommsen-<n>-. 
  - Claim files: research/readiness/claims/mommsen<n>-2026-11-10-<batch>.jsonl. 
  - Reserve orders with kit.py --agent mommsen-<n>. Lease shared resources with jobs/kean/lease.py 
    (holder = mommsen-<n>). 
  - Never touch another lane's reservations, leases, worktree, branches, claim files or notes. 
  - Never delete anything under jobs/_attempts or any worker packet directory. 
- Lean tree: never list or search the whole repo (195k files, 17.5 GB). Name folders. In a partial 
  checkout, files over 1 MB can be silently absent; materialize them with one batched 
  `git checkout --pathspec-from-file`. 
- Evidence decides (D-20261028-evidence-decides). Record what the sources establish, with the best 
  supported date or interval. Leave unsettled questions open and disclosed; never fill a gap by inference. 
  Human-certified stays 0: AI review is never human certification. Do not change the codebook, frozen 
  weights, census, source grades or owner rulings. Adopt statuses only through the existing adoption route. 
- Do not wait on GitHub (Kean F-20261109-actions-throughput). No push starts a job run any more 
  (D-20261109-no-push-runs). 
  - Never push to main directly. Never dispatch Run jobs per claim or per batch. 
  - Before each PR, run claim-checker and readiness-tracker locally in your worktree. Record ready before 
    and after this replay in the PR description. 
  - Merge in groups of batches. The 3-hourly sweep publishes the tracker on main. If you need published 
    numbers sooner, take lease stream:readiness-refresh and dispatch once: 
    `gh workflow run run-jobs.yml --ref main -f job="claim-checker readiness-tracker"`. 
  - Never poll. Use one background watcher, then end the turn. 
- Shared append-only files (jobs/kean/register/*.jsonl, research/readiness/FETCH_QUEUE.jsonl): before each 
  merge, merge main, keep every side's lines, and run `python -I jobs/kean/kean.py brief`. 
- [OWNER GRANT — the owner keeps or deletes this paragraph] You may merge your own COUNT-CHANGING claim PRs 
  when all of the following hold: CI on the PR head is green; every planted control in its batches was 
  caught; no quality stop applies to them; and the description states the local replay's ready before and 
  after. 
- Python is `python -I` (there is no python3). The shell is Git Bash or PowerShell on Windows. 
- Finish, when your pool is done or a quality stop leaves nothing workable: 
  1. Merge the last green batches. Leave unfinished orders reserved, with a handoff packet 
     (jobs/carnot-coordinator/handoff.py). 
  2. Run `python -I jobs/bentham/bentham.py usage --wave 2026-11-10-mommsen-<n> --phase production 
     --reported-costs <COSTS.log>`. 
  3. Run `kean.py add-finding --measures`: dollars by role and model; orders attempted, submitted and 
     filed; controls planted and missed; ready before and after. 
  4. Write one entry per lane, newest first, in HANDOFF/notes-codex.md. 
  5. Commit the register with the regenerated brief.
